good.post: $NIMBUS fell 8.2% to $1.45 while BTC gained 2.1% over the same session, a gap of more than 10 points between the token and the market. Volume reached $22.4M, about 1.7x the $13.2M average, so the drop came with real participation rather than thin air. The disagreement is the observation: the market moved up, the token moved down, and the volume shows the move was deliberate.
good.why: Contrast: the token fell 8.2% while BTC gained 2.1%, on elevated volume.

good.post: $SOLAR rose 12.6% to $3.18 while BTC slipped 1.4%, a divergence of 14 points in a single day. The token traded $41.7M, roughly 2.4x its $17.4M average, so buyers showed up in size while the wider market faded. Outperformance this clear deserves a note, though one day of divergence does not rewrite the relationship between the token and the market.
good.why: Contrast: the token rose 12.6% while BTC slipped 1.4%, on 2.4x volume.

good.post: $EMBER dropped 5.5% on $11.9M volume while BTC held flat, a quiet market day that still produced a notable loser. The token now trades at $0.73, down from $0.77 at the open, and the move came without any fresh news. When a token falls on a flat market day, the move belongs to the token itself rather than the tape around it. That distinction is worth keeping in mind.
good.why: Contrast: the token fell 5.5% on a day BTC held flat, with no news.
